Be clear, I don't have any problem with depicting serious issues in a comedic context. I think there's plenty of ways to do that effectively and tastefully, and I could definitely get on board. So then why did the tone of this show give me such a sense of cognitive dissonance? So I've been reflecting on my reaction for the past few days, and I think it's that the commentary and the comedy were not working together the way I think I wanted them to. And again, I don't have a problem with the fact that it's a comedy, and I also get that part of the point of the humor is That in horror, it's common when you're dealing with such an extreme, fantastical premise that it's kind of hard to ask the audience to take it too seriously. So you kind of wanna lean into camp factor and the humor that is kind of organically coming up naturally anyway. But that doesn't really feel like the case here. Like, the comedic tone feels very conspicuously, deliberately crafted. Like, it was funny and campy one moment, and then it was absolutely horrifying the next. And again, to be clear, I'm mostly not talking about the body horror. I'm talking about, like, emotional and psychological abuse. The stuff that feels more real. And the funny stuff was making me laugh, while the horrifying stuff was doing most of the heavy lifting to convey the themes and messaging. But if the purpose of the comedy was to be satirical or to, like, Rob the toxic culture of its power, like comedy sometimes attempts to do, if that was the goal, I don't think it really gelled for me. And, like, if it were just a horror story about a girl with teeth in her vagina, that might be fine. But the subject matter surrounding it is so intrinsically loaded and depicted so vividly in such a viscerally unsettling way, that what I found to be, like, the disconnect between the comedic tone and, like, the thematic point of the story was a bit of a problem for me. But if this show seems Up your alley. And if you think you can handle the body horror, I would still recommend seeing it, because I think it's a show that will elicit strong reactions that will vary a lot from person to person and whether or not you're laughing. Either way, it's definitely a compelling watch.
